Close neighbours.
Different centres.

A source-first comparison of public materials. Product descriptions are observations from the linked sources. The differentiation is our interpretation, not a benchmark verdict.

ProductWhat its source presentsCentre of gravity

opencompany

Its public site calls it a multiplayer AI workspace with a self-building wiki, workflows, model-agnostic sessions, connected sources and cloud sandboxes.

Observed centre: a shared workspace where humans and agents run company processes.

Primary site ↗

Lindy

Its public site presents an “AI teammate” that connects to company tools, knows company context and does work for a team. It visibly promotes integrations and a hosted sign-up.

Observed centre: tool-connected AI teammates and automation for business functions.

Primary site ↗

CrewAI

Its documentation describes an open-source framework that combines structured, event-driven Flows with autonomous agent Crews.

Observed centre: developer orchestration of multi-agent applications and workflows.

Primary docs ↗

Restless

Our intended product is a control plane for owner/operators. It delegates outcomes through accountable leads, real Staff production and a persistent runtime.

Intended centre: useful company output per unit of scarce owner attention.

Product boundary ↗

Our interpretation

The difference is where the owner stands.

Restless is not centred on a workspace to inhabit, a set of AI teammates to configure, or a framework to build. It is centred on delegating a whole outcome and receiving the prepared last mile.

This comparison does not establish relative quality, availability or fit. We did not run these products in a common benchmark. Public materials can change after the observation date.
